claims.sourceText: NASA SP-5110, 55-Nitinol: The Alloy With a Memory, Battelle Memorial Institute for NASA, 1972, chapter 1 p. 1 and references 12 and 74, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19720022818/downloads/19720022818.pdf ; NASA CR-1433, Nitinol Characterization Study, September 1969, foreword p. iii and p. 2, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19690026989/downloads/19690026989.pdf ; US Patent 3,174,851, https://patents.google.com/patent/US3174851A/en
claims.text: The federal literature on nitinol, one report of it written by Battelle itself, does not support a Battelle 1948-49 lineage for the alloy. NASA SP-5110, prepared for NASA by Battelle Memorial Institute in 1972, opens: 'Some 10 years ago, Buehler and Wiley of the U.S. Naval Ordnance Laboratory developed a series of engineering alloys that possess a unique mechanical (shape) memory. The generic name of the series of alloys is 55-Nitinol, where Nitinol stands for Nickel Titanium Naval Ordnance Laboratory.' The earliest Naval Ordnance Laboratory nitinol report cited anywhere in its reference list is NOLTR 61-75 of 3 August 1961; US Patent 3,174,851 was filed on 1 December 1961; and NASA CR-1433 of September 1969 records Battelle's own role as a subcontractor to Goodyear Aerospace which 'processed the basic Nitinol rod'. The allegation that Wright-Patterson-sponsored Battelle reports on nickel-titanium alloy from 1948-49 are missing from Air Force and Battelle archives is kept on this board as the allegation it is, and is unsupported by the federal literature opened here.

claims.sourceText: NASA CR-1433, Nitinol Characterization Study, Goodyear Aerospace Corporation report GER 14188 under contract NAS 1-7522 for NASA Langley Research Center, September 1969, Foreword p. iii and p. 2. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19690026989/downloads/19690026989.pdf
claims.text: Battelle's documented role in the alloy is late and contractual. NASA CR-1433 of September 1969 records that the nitinol was 'supplied by Mr. William J. Buehler of the Magnetism and Metallurgy Division of the U.S. Naval Ordnance Laboratory (NOL), Silver Spring, Maryland', and that 'As subcontractor to GAC, Battelle Memorial Institute (BMI), Columbus, Ohio, processed the basic Nitinol rod'. The same report calls the NOL work 'the recent discovery'.
